themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Pile Up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 4 this past week versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—suggesting a sudden clustering of derelict bicycles in Washington Heights/Inwood that warrants street-level investigation into whether this reflects a new dumping pattern, bike-share maintenance failure, or theft recovery sites.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike)
Z-score of 7.49 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Spike is recent: emerged within last 7 days
reporting_angles: Map the 4 complaints geographically—are they clustered in one neighborhood block or dispersed?
Contact Citi Bike operations and NYPD to determine if this reflects bike-share dysfunction, theft chop-shops, or illegal dumping

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped to 13 this past week versus a 5.6-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 131% increase (z-score: 3.82)—indicating emerging garbage or recycling management problems in apartment buildings that align with the Community Board's longstanding request for more frequent litter basket collection.
evidence: 13 residential disposal complaints last week vs. 5.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (131% spike)
Z-score of 3.82 indicates statistically significant deviation
Converges with Community Board's repeated budget request for 'more frequent litter basket collection'
reporting_angles: Interview residents and building supers about what disposal problems they're reporting—overflowing bins, missed pickups, or contamination?
Cross-check with Sanitation Department schedules to see if collection frequency has changed or if specific blocks are underserved

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Concerns Emerge
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints spiked to 4 complaints 2 weeks ago versus a 1.0-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 300% increase (z-score: 4.24)—suggesting a possible foodborne illness cluster or food vendor hygiene issue; timing and scale warrant Department of Health follow-up, especially given the concurrent 2300% spike in mobile food vendor complaints.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike)
Z-score of 4.24 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Concurrent spike: mobile food vendor complaints up 2300% (3 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline), suggesting possible vendor-related contamination source
reporting_angles: Obtain Department of Health inspection records for mobile food vendors in the district over the past 2–3 weeks—were violations or closures issued?
Interview poisoning complainants to identify common food sources, vendors, or locations and determine if outbreak is linked to a single operator

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints skyrocketed to 3 complaints 3 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—indicating either rapid expansion of unlicensed or non-compliant street food operations in Washington Heights/Inwood, or a spike in resident concerns about vendor behavior.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 is the highest statistical signal in the dataset
Correlates with food poisoning spike (4 complaints 2 weeks ago), suggesting health/safety nexus
reporting_angles: Street reporting: identify which blocks or intersections are seeing new mobile food vendors and whether they are licensed with Department of Health
Interview Department of Health about enforcement activity—have they received complaints or conducted enforcement sweeps in the district recently?

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 18 this past 3 weeks ago versus a 2.2-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 8.49)—suggesting emerging issues with Uber, Lyft, or other ride-sharing services (illegal pickups, congestion, reckless driving, or unlicensed operators) that warrant inquiry into street-level enforcement and licensing compliance.
evidence: 18 for-hire vehicle complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 8.49 indicates highly significant anomaly
Spike is recent: appeared within last 3 weeks
reporting_angles: Contact TLC (Taxi & Limousine Commission) to determine if there has been a surge in unlicensed for-hire vehicle activity or enforcement actions in the district
Interview residents and local business owners about what specific for-hire vehicle behaviors (blocking streets, double-parking, reckless driving) are prompting complaints
